fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Internal Drive Aisle; Landscaped Area; Front Entry Area; Pedestrian Walkways; Street Frontage; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Congestion
fr.recommendations: Based on the observed site characteristics, maintaining clear and unobstructed pathways through the multiple access points could improve responder ingress and egress efficiency. Vehicle congestion within the parking areas and drive aisle may impede apparatus movement and staging, so keeping travel lanes clear would support effective maneuvering around the main building. Limited access to the rear of the structure may benefit from pre-incident familiarization by local responders to support navigation during operations. Dense vegetation along landscaped areas and open green spaces could reduce visibility for approaching personnel, and periodic management of vegetation near the front entry and pedestrian walkways may enhance situational awareness and movement corridors throughout the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Irrigated Landscape; Vegetation Adjacent to Access Route; Limited Defensible Space; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing direct vegetation contact with the structure and creating greater separation between brush, shrubs, and building surfaces could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity in the immediate structure zone. Where tree clusters are present, thinning to increase spacing between canopies and removing lower limbs may reduce vertical fuel continuity and support suppression operations. Managing scattered shrubs and mixed vegetation cover across the property, particularly where it connects fuel from open terrain toward the structure, would help interrupt fuel pathways. Vegetation growing adjacent to the access route should be trimmed back to maintain clearance along both sides, which would support firefighter access and improve navigation during suppression operations. Expanding and maintaining the irrigated landscape zone around the structure may provide a useful buffer that reduces fuel continuity near improvements. Continued long-term vegetation management across the property, including periodic reassessment of regrowth near the structure perimeter, could improve overall wildfire resilience.
